findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed shutting the faucet with bare hands after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that a barrier is used to shut the facet after handwashing to avoid recontaminating your clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was no sani bucket observed in the kitchen as food prep began. Discussed with PIC. Inspector asked PIC to have a Sani bucket made. The Sanitizer for the sani bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer is always made and placed in a sani bucket before any food prep or handling at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the certified food manager’s allergen training certification. PIC told inspector that they had the training done but they cannot find it now however, they will look through their documents and find the certification. Ensure that all paperwork are available and accessible for viewing and verification at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.comment:

7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

On arrival the spray bottle used for sanitizing bleached out the test strip used by the inspector. The bottle was remade during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

During this inspection the CFPM for the facility was not present during preparation operations/ food handling. As a class-II facility the CFPM should be available at all times of operation. Ensure that there are enough CFPM so that one is available at all times the kitchen is in operation. CFPM arrived at the end of the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

No reporting agreements were available for food handlers during this inspection. Clean copies were given during this inspection and food employees signed fresh copies during this inspection to correct.  Ensure that copies are maintained at the facility moving forward.

findings.comment:

When the manager arrived they were able to work on the machine and found the issue. By the end of the inspection the machine was operating correctly.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

The hand sink in the dish area is without hand soap during this inspection. Hand soap was provided during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Rodent feces observed on the floor of the storage area in the kitchen. Clean floors to eliminate feces. Enlist pest control to prevent presence of pests.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Coving in the prep kitchen observed missing (behind the slicer/stand mixer) or pulling away from the wall (near the dish machine). Replace or repair coving.
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. [C]

Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
No written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Inspector will email policy. Print and post or keep on file for reference in case of vomit/diarrhea events.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  [Pf]
